targetAudience.primary: Architects and operations leaders managing multi-agent teams, failover, and worker replacement
targetAudience.knowledgeAssumption: The reader understands role-based assignment, handoffs, team state, and operational recovery.
targetAudience.readerProblem: A replacement agent can match the outgoing worker's model, role, and tools yet still disrupt a team's learned coordination conventions.

whyNow: A controlled agent-interchangeability study reports that role-matched swaps preserve much task outcome while increasing communication cost per unit of progress by roughly 16–63%, with coordination efficiency recovering later than task score.

externalHook.description: The replacement completes the task, so the system closes recovery while the team is still spending materially more coordination effort.

coreProposition: Role and capability qualification do not establish destination-team compatibility; replacement activation requires separate evidence for team coordination, carried-state scope, and recovery of both outcome and coordination efficiency.

originalValue.description: Reframes replacement from individual capability matching into destination-team re-admission with scoped relationship state and a two-dimensional recovery window.

readerTakeaway: Bind replacement evidence to the destination team and seat, separate task knowledge from relationship-specific state, and keep recovery open until both task outcomes and coordination costs stabilize.

supported: The primary study reports substantial communication-cost penalties after role-matched swaps despite preserved task performance.
Partner specificity increases with coupling and formation history in the reported ablations.
Task outcome can recover earlier than coordination efficiency.
unsupported: A claim that all team memory must be cleared
General proof for large organizations or crash-time failover
uncertain: How to version live team coordination state
How to measure compatibility in teams larger than two
Which relationship memories should survive emergency replacement

firstPartyRole.rationale: The argument stands on public primary research and is useful without reference to any first-party system.

decisionReason: The designed comparisons support a bounded distinction between role qualification and team qualification with direct operational consequences.
